sentence: The UK Chief Medical Officers advise adults not to regularly drink more than 14 units a week, spread over three days or more.
note: CMOs: not regularly drink more than 14 units per week; spread evenly over 3 days or more

sentence: The UK Chief Medical Officers advise that adults should not regularly drink more than 14 units of alcohol a week.
note: CMO guidance 14 units per week

sentence: Their guidance says there is no completely safe level of regular drinking, because no level of regular consumption improves health.
note: There is no definitively safe lower limit, no level of regular consumption improves health

sentence: One unit is 10 millilitres, or 8 grams, of pure alcohol, and the strength printed on a label as ABV can be used to work out units.
note: One unit is 10ml of pure alcohol (8g); ABV on labels

sentence: For anyone who is pregnant or could become pregnant, the Chief Medical Officers advise that the safest approach is not to drink alcohol at all.
note: If pregnant or think you could become pregnant, the safest approach is not to drink alcohol at all

sentence: The UK Chief Medical Officers advise that, to keep the risk of harm from alcohol low, adults should not regularly drink more than 14 units a week.
note: CMOs advise adults should not regularly drink more than 14 units per week

sentence: For someone who drinks as much as 14 units, the advice is to spread it evenly over three days or more.
note: If someone drinks up to 14 units, best to spread evenly over 3 days or more

sentence: The guidance also says there is no definitively safe lower limit, because no level of regular drinking improves health.
note: No definitively safe lower limit; no level of regular alcohol consumption improves health

sentence: Some older leaflets still quote daily limits, but the weekly figure is the one in the current guidance.
note: Search summary: some older pages still quote daily limits of 2-3 and 3-4 units; weekly 14-unit figure is current

sentence: One unit is 10 millilitres of pure alcohol, which is 8 grams.
note: NHS leaflet: one unit is 10ml of pure alcohol (8g)

sentence: The strength of a drink is shown on the label as alcohol by volume, or ABV.
note: ABV is usually printed on can and bottle labels

sentence: Units can be worked out by multiplying the volume in millilitres by the ABV percentage and dividing by 1,000.
note: Multiply volume in ml by ABV and divide by 1,000

sentence: Using that method, a pint of strong lager at 5.2% ABV comes to about three units.
note: Example: pint (568ml) of 5.2% lager = 2.95 units

sentence: As a guide, 14 units is about six pints of average-strength beer or six medium glasses of average-strength wine.
note: 14 units equals six pints of 4% beer or six medium (175ml) glasses of 13% wine

sentence: The Chief Medical Officers' guidance links regular drinking above the low-risk level with a range of long-term conditions, including seven types of cancer, heart disease, high blood pressure, diabetes and mental health problems.
note: Sticking to guidelines helps keep risk low from ... long-term health conditions including seven types of cancer, heart disease, high blood pressure, diabetes and mental health problems

sentence: It also names accidents and injuries, alcohol poisoning and harm from violence or abuse among the short-term risks.
note: accidents and injuries, physical or sexual abuse, alcohol poisoning

sentence: Drinking a large amount in a short time carries a particular risk of alcohol poisoning.
note: Risk of alcohol poisoning when many units are drunk over a short period

sentence: Mouth cancers are more common among people who drink, and the risk is higher still when drinking is combined with smoking or any form of tobacco.
note: Significantly increased risk of oral cancers among drinkers, particularly with smoking or tobacco

sentence: The 2016 review behind the guidance estimated that the lifetime risk of dying from an alcohol-related condition is around 1 per cent, or a little under, for people drinking at the low-risk level.
note: Per the 2016 review, risk of dying from an alcohol-related condition around or a little under 1% over a lifetime at the low-risk level

sentence: Heavier drinking raises the risk further.
note: Drinking more heavily raises risks further

sentence: The guidance is therefore described as a way to keep risk low, not to remove it.
note: Guidelines keep risk low; no safe level

sentence: For anyone who is pregnant or thinks they could become pregnant, the Chief Medical Officers advise that the safest approach is not to drink alcohol at all.
note: If pregnant or think you could become pregnant, safest approach is not to drink alcohol at all

sentence: Signs listed as a reason to seek support include drinking more over time, struggling to cut down, poor sleep, thinking ahead to the next drink, risky behaviour and concern from other people.
note: Warning signs: increased consumption, struggling to cut down, poor sleep, anticipating the next drink, risky behaviour, concern from others

sentence: The NHS Better Health site points people to their local alcohol support service, or to Drinkline on 0300 123 1110, which it describes as free, confidential help for anyone concerned about their own or someone else's drinking.
note: Find your local alcohol support service or call Drinkline on 0300 123 1110 for free, confidential help

sentence: It also offers the NHS Drink Free Days app for setting a weekly unit target.
note: Use the NHS Drink Free Days app to set a weekly unit target

sentence: NHS pages describe a drinks diary as a way to see how much is being drunk, in which situations, and how cutting down could start.
note: NHS alcohol misuse guidance: a diary gives a good idea of how much, situations, how you could start to cut down

sentence: Having several alcohol-free days each week is another suggestion, as are eating before drinking, choosing lower-strength drinks and diluting drinks.
note: NHS 111 Wales: several alcohol-free days; trusts: eating before drinking, lower-strength drinks, diluting

sentence: The NHS says treatment for alcohol use disorder is available from a GP or a specialist alcohol service.
note: NHS: you can get treatment for alcohol-use disorder from your GP or a specialist alcohol addiction service

sentence: Options it lists include counselling, self-help groups, talking therapies such as CBT, and medicines.
note: Treatment options listed: counselling incl. self-help groups and talking therapies such as CBT; medicines

sentence: Alcoholics Anonymous, Al-Anon UK and SMART Recovery are named as support groups.
note: Support groups mentioned: AA, Al-Anon UK, SMART Recovery

sentence: The NHS says a person who is not ready to stop, or who only wants to cut down, will be supported to reduce drinking to a safer level.
note: If not ready to stop yet or just want to cut down, you will be supported to reduce drinking to a safer level

sentence: A Scottish NHS leaflet for heavier drinkers warns against stopping suddenly, because withdrawal symptoms can follow, and says symptoms such as shakes or sweats call for NHS 111 or urgent medical attention.
note: Leaflet: do not stop drinking suddenly; gradual cut down; shakes or sweats should prompt a call to 111 or urgent medical attention
